name: memory.worldclass
description: Judge one RIG Memory OS process, result, or outcome against the world-class ladder. State = evidence dump (config, live status, tests, outputs). Score is the maturity rung; the 0.9 bar is maturity >= 3.6/4.

maturity.instructions: Maturity of this component given the evidence
criteria: Broken, absent, or silently failing -- it does not produce what it promises
Manually drivable only -- works when a human runs it, no schedule, no monitoring
Scheduled and observed -- runs unattended, logs exist, failures surface and the last tick is green
Best practice -- contract documented, failures alert, plant-tested or receipt-proven, honest status separate from loaded, idempotent where it should be
World class -- outcomes measured against a north-star metric, self-healing within named bounds, calibration or feedback loop feeding improvements, evidence queryable by downstream consumers

verified.instructions: The evidence contains proof this component actually produces its claimed output (command output, row counts, log lines, test results) rather than config or intent alone

trustworthy_output.instructions: A downstream consumer (agent, dashboard, human) can treat this component's output as true without re-checking it

gap_action.instructions: The single most effective action to raise this component to the best-practice rung

criteria.none: Already at best practice or world class
criteria.fix_config: A stale binding, dead path, wrong profile, or missing env value explains the failure
criteria.fix_code: A real defect in shipped code must be repaired
criteria.build_missing: The capability does not exist yet and must be built
criteria.await_time: A time-gated release condition (observation window, calibration corpus) is the only blocker; nothing to repair

rules.reason: below best-practice rung -- belongs on the fix-or-build list
claim rests on config/intent, not on produced evidence
